title: Restore trustworthy four-module runtime E2E evidence after patched Go compiler upgrade
goal: Unblock global security CI after GO-2026-6809 Go 1.26.10 fix by verifying exactly pinned go.mod old/new Git blobs in four legacy source-attested Go runtimes and rerunning full module tests and go vet; retain historical audit SHA and all mandatory vuln scanners unchanged.
invariants: Historical VERIFIED runtime and performance SHAs and old reports remain immutable; no source or product contract changed in this child PR
Only one Go module declaration per protected runtime is allowed to differ; both former and patched Git blobs must match independently verified Go 1.26.8->Go 1.26.10 transition.
Any unexpected source file, module content, module count, branch ancestry or hash mismatch fails before testing.
Every changed module has fresh complete go test -count=1 ./... and go vet ./... under CI-local patched Go toolchain, then retains preexisting contract/adversarial/performance mandatory audit.
The emitted runtime_unchanged_since_* fields are false on patched runtimes, never mislabeled true; unmodified sources still report true.
Mandatory CHK-SCA-GO, CHK-SAST-GO and all other security gates are not waived, skipped, or downgraded.
security_properties: No client permission source changes, new IAM, tenant rules or runtime dependencies.
Only four reviewed runtime modules are allowed in the static trusted-delta map; other runtimes fail closed.
Static allowed blobs are one-time version-specific; future compiler upgrades require new independent proof, not an automatic go.mod exemption.

migration.rationale: Dev-engine evidence checker only, no product runtime modification or schema migration.

rollback.strategy: Revert only new source-checker changes to historical strict identity rule, preserving blocked outcome until separately approved proof exists.

inputs: PR #196 Go 1.26.10 compiler-only security upgrade with Go module allowlist and historic E2E failure on exact SHA
Documented source proof SHAs in source runtime PROGRESS for CAP-INV-002/004/005/006
Parent engineering E4-SEC-002B and SCAID IMPLEMENTED but not yet CI-VERIFIED
outputs: One shared fail-closed source identity validator for four modules, distinct old/patched byte fingerprints and mandatory fresh module tests/vet
Four E2E audit summaries truthfully set runtime unchanged=false only when patch applied
Negative Git fixture tests for allowlisted module, invalid type/path/contents and unchanged ancestor
acceptance_tests: Every module old/new blob pair exactly matches original and candidate evidence and no other Event Search/Inspection/Hunt/Saved file changes are ignored.
Git synthetic source-only module upgrade passes identity, alternative future compiler and extra executable source are refused.
Exact final SHA CHK-EVENT-INSPECTION-E2E, CHK-EVENT-SEARCH-E2E, CHK-HUNT-MANAGEMENT-E2E, CHK-SAVED-QUERY-ASSETS-E2E pass without stale VERIFIED claims.
Full mandatory CHK-SCA-GO on patched stdlib and all global format/coverage/security gates pass on same final SHA.
Command and Timeline runtime cross-platform tests remain green; no production security claim beyond tested code.
definition_of_ready: Go compiler patch #196 exists with exact original and patched source commit/blob identity; failing E2E source identity proven by exact GitHub CI
No modification to product behavior needed; evidence reconciliation task under security parent only
definition_of_done: Byte-pinned evidence transition and fresh Go module tests plus vet verified on exact head
Mandatory engineering-kernel, Command and Timeline CI successful on exact SHA
Handoff documents historical statuses, reviewer and merge dependency; no false full product VERIFIED/ACCEPTED claim

performance_budget.rationale: Only existing CI-time Go module test/vet executions; product runtime code and budgets are unchanged.
